rubric_additions.rubric-9: Resolve effective Python runner precedence: FLASK_RUN_RELOAD=false does not override make dev's explicit --reload. A no-reload claim requires a supported effective flag/configuration; otherwise scope evidence to the actual reload worker and process-group cleanup. Preserve existing reload policy unless selected for change; an environment assignment alone cannot establish single-process startup.
rubric_additions.rubric-10: For the selected Python metric-reader settings, preserve supported fractional values and the SDK's invalid/empty-input handling. Any short-run timing defaults belong only to the selected launch policy.
rubric_additions.rubric-11: For a selected Python zero-code CLI, resolve the installed exporter-list reader and alias-selected transport; protocol environment values need not control explicit OTLP aliases. Valid mixed lists containing supported OTLP members require approval/header checks, with selected conflict and approved signal A/unused generic B controls through the normal command. Isolate only added OTLP members, retaining other exporters and their bridge. Preserve the installed owner's whole-none, case, empty-member and duplicate behavior; retain source-proven unsupported combinations without another language's normalization or a replacement parser.
rubric_additions.rubric-20: For selected Python lazy native sinks, credit public standard-library logger/handler configuration that establishes each producer's detected route before root bridge installation. Inspecting private initialization may explain laziness; calling an underscored initializer solely to trigger lazy setup or a diagnostic cannot establish a supported bootstrap mechanism or preservation proof.
rubric_additions.rubric-23: The pristine fixture submits app.logger.warning to its executor without copying caller context. Audit plans acceptance for that missing boundary; instrumentation repairs it where still missing; verification checks the current request-to-async SDK-context join without editing. An already repaired current path is not a remaining missing-transfer defect.
rubric_additions.rubric-25: The Python fixture's operator telemetry-privacy contract covers existing exported HTTP SERVER spans as well as selected logs. A logging-only sanitizer cannot close span privacy. Allocate unmatched sensitive path/query and escaping-error cases to their actual producers and supported sanitization boundaries. Audit retains source-backed repairs and future controls; instrumentation/verification retain current normal-launch received server-span assertions and selected log evidence. Do not add payload/header capture, extra exception telemetry or blanket suppression. This policy is not a universal OpenTelemetry ban on exception messages or stacks.
rubric_additions.rubric-26: For the Python fixture's selected HTTP privacy path, retained fields include bounded error category, method/route/status, trace context and Resource identity. Use actual structured producer fields or message-template arguments with their source types, normalize only verified decoration, and bind every selected non-success/access/error operation to its native and exported category plus required typed fields.
rubric_additions.rubric-28: For a selected Python attribute sanitizer, inspect a downstream record after the actual callback. A plain mapping that loses existing SDK drop state is not unchanged default behavior; use that owner's supported mutation/snapshot contract without synthesizing counters. Rebuilding a parent span does not preserve each event's own attribute limits or accumulated dropped-attribute count.
rubric_additions.rubric-34: A selected Python metric reader's collection timeout is not automatically its transport timeout or the application stop budget.
rubric_additions.rubric-41: In Python standard logging, even a rejecting handler can prevent lastResort fallback. Bridge namespace exclusion therefore does not establish native diagnostics: inspect an eligible handler or supported suppression for the actual SDK logger namespace. Application/framework sibling handlers or a different internal recursion logger cannot supply that route. An adequate existing route or source-supported suppression requires neither a new handler nor a newly emitted diagnostic.
rubric_additions.rubric-49: For a selected manually constructed Python metric reader, omitted timing kwargs are not missing wiring when the actual installed constructor consumes the supported environment values.
